subject: PrivNet proxy timeouts impacting inference - WellPath
messages:
From: Aaron Li <aaron.li@wellpath.health>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: infra@wellpath.health
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PrivNet proxy timeouts impacting inference - WellPath

Hi Olga / Monica,

We started seeing elevated 504 / connection timeout errors to our private endpoint (wellpath-prod-1.redwood.local) starting ~04:30 UTC this morning. Latency spikes appear correlated with deployments to the PrivNet proxy fleet (we were testing the new proxy image rolled at 04:15).

Impact: ~18% of inference requests failing, primarily shorter sequences. We've attached a small error snippet and a sample request id for investigation. Our infra team is looped (infra@wellpath.health) and is available on a call if helpful.

Attached: wellpath-error-snippet-0429.txt

Can you confirm you see the same telemetry on your end and advise on immediate mitigation steps? This is affecting a live clinical triage feature so we want to prioritize.

Thanks,
Aaron
Aaron Li
Head of Platform Engineering
WellPath Health

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrivNet proxy timeouts impacting inference - WellPath

Team — internal notes / proposed technical approach (please reply-all with ETA):

What we see so far
- Timeline: new priv-proxy image v2.4.0 rolled starting ~04:15 UTC for WellPath's private fleet. Error onset ~04:30 UTC.
- Symptom: increased connection timeouts between runtime agents and proxy on short-lived connections. Failure mode looks like a connection pooling regression: proc table exhaustion + delayed TLS handshake retries under bursty auth refresh.
- Affected: only WellPath's private VPC (no global host issues).

Immediate mitigation options (pros/cons):
1) Roll back WellPath priv-proxy to v2.3.1 (fast; targeted; low blast radius) — recommended if we can do a per-customer rollout.
2) Increase proxy connection timeouts / reduce connection pooling aggressiveness (config change) — lower risk but may not fully mitigate handshake delay under load.
3) Force traffic through alternate proxy nodes (route-level failover) — depends on capacity.

Requesting: Rishi, please prepare a rollback to v2.3.1 for the WellPath proxy pool and run it on a single AZ first. Grace, please prepare to capture tcpdump + broker logs for the 04:15-05:00 UTC window and stash to S3. Monica, I’ll coordinate comms with Aaron and confirm the bridge at 10:15 PDT.

We should keep Aaron updated every 15 minutes until service stabilizes.

—Olga

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: Aaron Li <aaron.li@wellpath.health>, infra@wellpath.health
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrivNet proxy timeouts impacting inference - WellPath

On Thu, Apr 29, 2027 at 9:12 AM Aaron Li <aaron.li@wellpath.health> wrote:
> We started seeing elevated 504 / connection timeout errors to our private endpoint...

Quick update — rollback executed: per-customer rollback to priv-proxy v2.3.1 started at 10:22 PDT in AZ-a (canary), completed for all AZs at 10:48 PDT.

Observations:
- Error rates returned to baseline (~<1% failures) within ~3 minutes of completing the last AZ rollback.
- Collected logs and tcpdumps are uploaded: wellpath-debug-logs-0429.tar.gz (includes proxy logs, agent logs, pcap for 04:15-05:00 UTC).
- We flagged a kernel/backtrace pattern in the proxy process that points to a connection pooling edge case introduced by v2.4.0 connection re-use path.

Next steps (short):
- Grace to finish full log extraction and provide sanitized traces by EOD.
- We'll keep v2.3.1 pinned for WellPath until a patch release for 2.4.0 is validated (tentative remediation window 5/4).

Aaron — can you confirm you see recovery on your side and whether traffic looks healthy for the application?

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: Aaron Li <aaron.li@wellpath.health>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident summary: WellPath PrivNet proxy upgrade regression (Apr 29)

Aaron — attaching a short post-incident summary and next steps. Thank you and your infra team for the quick response and patience.

High-level summary:
- Incident window: 2027-04-29 04:30 UTC — 2027-04-29 10:48 UTC (service recovered after rollback).
- Impact: transient 504/timeouts for ~18% of inference requests to your private endpoint during the peak window.
- Root cause: a connection pooling regression in priv-proxy image v2.4.0 that under certain auth refresh patterns caused delayed TLS handshakes and connection exhaustion.

Actions taken:
- Immediate: per-customer rollback to stable image (v2.3.1) completed by 10:48 PDT, which restored baseline error rates. (Rishi-led)
- Diagnostic: collected logs and pcaps (wellpath-debug-logs-0429.tar.gz) and traced failing paths to a faulty connection re-use path in the proxy. (Grace-led)
- Remediation: engineering will ship a patched proxy image v2.4.1 that fixes the pooling logic; we plan a staged rollout with additional e2e auth stress tests. Target ship: 2027-05-04.
- Compensation: we're open to a service credit conversation given impact to your production feature — Monica will follow up with a formal proposal (cc).

Preventive changes (short term):
- Per-customer image pinning for private fleets during upgrade windows.
- Enhanced early-warning alerting for short-lived TLS handshake spikes.
- Improved rollforward/rollback automation so we can isolate customer fleets faster.

Attachments: postmortem-wellpath-privnet-0429.pdf
Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/WellPath-PrivNet-Incident-0429
JIRA: INF-4729

If you'd like a 30-minute run-through of the postmortem and planned mitigations, happy to schedule — available this week.

Thanks again,
Olga Petrov
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
